successCriteria: The earned cruush+ scratch-card popup fills the complete viewport on desktop and mobile. Members remain inside the popup until they finish its interactions, press Done, or use its existing Close control.
Recently Active remains centered on the desktop viewport with no panel, a profile panel, and a right page panel open.
The bottom navigation remains centered on the desktop viewport with no panel, a profile panel, and a right page panel open.
Failed seeded profile images render the existing profile-gradient fallback instead of a broken image icon.
Mobile Recently Active and bottom navigation positioning remain unchanged.
Settings offers Pop-ups and Full screen for desktop page layout, with Pop-ups as the default.
Feed, cruushes, messages, and profile follow the selected desktop page layout from the bottom navigation.
The saved desktop Pop-ups preference remains effective on desktop devices when the browser window is narrower than 1120px; viewport width alone does not force full-screen navigation.
Map top actions fit within narrow desktop and small-mobile viewports without horizontal clipping, overlap, or hidden controls.
The map always uses cruush's in-app vector theme. Alternate style URLs, raster tiles, CARTO tiles, and automatic theme fallbacks are unsupported and cannot replace it after a slow load or tile error.
Published Spots load and appear on the map by default, while opening the Spots control opens discovery without changing layer visibility.
The Spots Map Controls button uses its active treatment only when one or more Spot filters limit the visible Spot dataset.
The Map Controls Spots button keeps the approved places handoff icon until Julien supplies category-specific Spot icons.
Settings menu rows show only primary labels while actual setting pages retain feature descriptions.
Zoom never changes an individual member's coordinates; zoom may only cluster or uncluster members.
Map presence offers 1h, 3h, 6h, 8h, 12h, 24h, 48h, 3d, 4d, 5d, 6d, and 7d.
No labels is removed from Map presence because Dark Room owns the distance-label replacement.
Top navigation icon buttons never show a grey circle at rest or on hover. Their existing focus visibility and click areas remain available without a grey fill.

Crowd Mode keeps the deployed fixed controls in the dedicated Crowds sheet. Crowds has no top-navigation icon; the active Crowd notice remains available from Map Controls and uses the existing pre-Hydra Crowd icon.

DL Mode uses Julien's exact supplied balaclava-and-halo icon in white while inactive and the existing cruush gradient while active, preserving the approved top-navigation canvas and spacing until Julien selects dedicated DL Mode colors.
Bottom navigation icons have no resting grey circle and the Map tab uses Noun Project globe 7869983 in white and cruush-gradient states at a balanced 48px canvas.

Mile High Club uses the same exact plane geometry throughout. Every MHC surface uses the approved shaded white 3D plane, including the map animation, settings, and the glyph beside the active member's name on both their own profile and other member profiles.

The Mile High Club traveller animation uses the approved shaded white 3D plane, 18 contrail bands, a 0.52 moving span, 0.26 light-blue-to-white handoff, 0.20 blend, 0.55 hold, 0.72 plane scale, and 5200ms period. The contrail uses #DAF3FF, #A9DCF3, and #77B9DA before its white ending poofs. MHC side-badge and signal borders use #77B9DA unless Pulse temporarily applies lime.

Mile High Club accepts an address or GPS coordinates in the first location control, places Use my current location and Drop my pin here directly below it, renders the selected pin with the canonical cruush heart instead of a circle, and lets the map fill the remaining screen down to the fixed bottom navigation.
The Mile High Club picker keeps its MapLibre host at the full visible picker height and resizes it with the layout, so the map renders instead of leaving a blank framed area.
The in-app Ghost Mode glyph uses the same exact electric-blue fading ghost shown by the map rotation fly-out.
Signup shows required Terms of Service and Privacy Policy checkboxes plus the optional cruush product-updates checkbox directly below the password fields.
The local 1.6 frontend can target its dedicated seeded API without reusing another worktree's port, so authenticated settings requests do not fail origin validation.
The local 1.6 frontend uses a worktree-local Vite dependency cache and one React runtime even when node_modules is shared with another worktree.
The current user's Dark Room heart renders the exact same shared keyhole and eye paths used by the Dark Room navigation icon, with the heart-pin keyhole filled solid black.
The Pulse EKG is vertically centered and spans the complete 80px heart width, with its path reaching both horizontal edges.
The Dark Room navigation mark punches its keyhole through the chapel at zero opacity while retaining the shared eye shape; only the heart-pin keyhole is filled solid black.
Every top-navigation glyph uses the same 40px mobile and 44px desktop canvas as DL Mode.
Top and right map controls paint above panels and marker previews, intercept pointer input, and prevent covered markers from previewing or opening.
Messages and Cruushes reserve the fixed bug-button position at the far right of their header action groups, keeping their settings buttons fully visible to its left.
Incoming, Sent, Mutual, and Views use one identical Cruushes row grid; mobile actions stay on the first row and each vibe capsule fits its own text below.
Selected sent and mutual cruush controls use the dark gradient and remain actionable so a second click unsends or removes the mutual.
Cruushes shows the permission-resolved distance beside activity time, using the member's mutual distance when available and Nearby otherwise.
Conversation settings uses the standard cruush Settings glyph, and the composer timer menu opens upward.
Cruushes uses the same segmented tab treatment as Messages, and switching Incoming, Sent, Mutual, or Views changes only the listed people and state-specific content inside the unchanged card grid.
Messages profile previews use the Cruushes card structure, use the same content slot that Feed uses for post text, omit vibe capsules, and retain Delete in the card corner.
Feed places a Seeking control beside Feed Settings. Its in-panel search field filters Feed posts by post content without opening another popup.

Seeking includes a profile keyword search that matches visible names, bios, and configured profile keywords such as kinks. Visibility includes the same search field with inverse meaning: matching people are excluded from seeing the member.
Messages and Cruushes place the full-screen page name directly beside Back while preserving the reserved bug-button slot.

Cruushes puts name and pronouns together in a full-width mobile content row above the action trio, puts Last online and Distance on separate lines beside the vertically centered action trio, and omits vibe capsules.
Profile actions remain one line in this exact order: cruush, Pin that user, Message. Pin remains visibly present but disabled when precise location is unavailable.
Every person-to-person Message action uses the arrow/send glyph. The bottom-navigation Messages glyph is never reused for a person action.
Every actionable cruush control is reversible from the same surface. Sent and Mutual states remain actionable so a second press unsends or removes the mutual.
After an unsend or mutual removal completes, the same cruush control immediately returns to the bright available gradient state.
Feed uses the approved winged-heart icon. Every person-to-person cruush control, including Mutual, uses the approved double-heart icon and never falls back to the Feed icon.
The signed-in member's profile popup and full profile show Signal and Vibes over the profile photo only. They do not repeat below About.
The local development seed gives several mutual-capable profiles precise-location sharing so an enabled Cruushes pin action can be tested without changing production data.
The landing tagline and NYC OPEN BETA capsule gain a white glow only while hovered, with their resting appearance unchanged.
Cruushes count and tab bars size only from the viewport or containing desktop panel, never from the active tab's row count.
Seeking Filters and Visibility Controls always render above both fixed navigation bars.
Seeking Filters can show only active Mile High Club members, and Visibility Controls can hide the member from active Mile High Club members; both controls live under Intimacy.
Visibility Controls does not duplicate the approximate distance-label preference owned by Map presence.
Profile editing links directly to the current Your side badges page and never renders the superseded intermediate badge page.

The current release offers only the Circle side-badge border. The border picker is absent and every legacy or saved frame renders as Circle. Custom border code and assets remain dormant for possible later work.
The Badge editor Save control matches Edit Profile Save and occupies the popup header's far-right action position.
Badge titles show the meaning without the Hanky color name. What this side says offers Give, Receive, Switch, Service, and Stone as independent intent choices.
The embedded Badge editor provides working Back and Close controls that both return to Edit Profile inside the same popup.
The Badge editor has no Remove Hanky action; selecting another badge replaces the Hanky on that side.
Badge selections remain local drafts until Save succeeds. Back, Close, browser unload, and Badge links that leave the editor ask the member to save when changes are pending.
The lime Hanky meaning is Mutual masturbation.

Vibes removes E-Girl/E-Boy; Style & Energy adds Blue-collar and Discreet; Scenes adds Collegiate; Archetypes adds Bull and Trade.
The Circle side-badge border has a solid black interior, keeps its icon centered without touching the frame, and floats close to the profile heart without overlapping it.
Hanky artwork fills the Circle border's interior and is clipped completely inside its stroke.
Dominant uses the established BDSM badge chevron glyph, empty for Dominant and filled for Dominant, taken. It does not use a generic heraldic shield or the dormant Diamond border geometry.
The dark pink Hanky meaning is Nipples/tits, replacing Tit torture.

Submissive uses an unfilled circle ring and Submissive, taken uses a filled circle. Dominant uses the empty BDSM chevron and Dominant, taken uses the filled BDSM chevron. Top and Bottom use only a plain upward or downward arrow. Badge icons remain centered and clear of the Circle frame.
Badge previews use the Dark Room purple gradient only when baseMode is STEALTH; Ghost Mode alone never recolors badge borders purple.
The Badge editor preview and map use the same side-badge size and offset. Saving side badges updates the signed-in map pin immediately, including while Dark Room is active.
Default left Role and right Position badges use the exact Badge-menu glyph and frame language, including the Switch hexagon, rather than alternate map-only icons.

Hovering either side badge on the signed-in member's map pin, another member's map pin, or a profile badge preview shows that specific badge's user-visible label. Leaving the badge clears the label, and the label never intercepts pointer input or opens the profile.

Every side-badge border is fully opaque. Signed-in user badges are indigo, mutual badges are purple, other-member badges are pink, active Mile High Club member badges are #77B9DA sky blue, Pulse badges are lime, Ghost decoy badges are Ghost blue, and Dark Room signed-in badges use the approved Dark Room gradient. These state colors apply consistently on map pins, profile previews, Cruushes, Messages, Feed, and other people listings.

Hanky colors use white for bondage, lime for mutual masturbation, orange for anytime/anywhere, dark blue for fucking, teal for tribbing/frotting, light pink for mommy, purple for toys, tan for heavy petting, lavender for crossdressing, mint green for discreet, and gold for threesomes/groups, with black paisley on white and tan.
Notifications is the far-right icon inside the desktop map top-navigation pill, immediately after Settings.
The deferred Hydra Crowd icon does not render in 1.6. The top navigation has no Crowd control.

Ghost Mode decoys carry decoy side badges in the same electric-blue treatment as the decoy heart, and active plus fly-out Ghost icons use the exact supplied /Volumes/good/ghost-mode-icon-final.svg asset.

The signed-in member's Ghost decoy keeps both side badges and its profile photo beneath the active Ghost icon treatment: dark blue at the top, electric blue through the middle, full opacity through halfway down, then one smooth fade to 10% opacity at the bottom. Both decoy badges share that same opacity fade. The profile photo uses the exact regular-heart clip and never paints above or beyond the heart border. Hover shows the live time remaining until rotation, and the decoy plays the existing last-minute Ghost animation for its owner. The real signed-in pin and other members remain unchanged.

Pride uses the supplied linked-symbol mark for T4T, uses clear purpose-drawn linked-symbol marks for Gay and Lesbian in the same visual family, replaces the rejected Nonbinary mark with a clear standard Nonbinary symbol, renames Both to Straight, removes Labrys plus Men and Women, and owns Trans and T4T instead of Community.

Superseded custom Heart, Diamond, Dom, Sub, and Switch frame implementations remain dormant in source for possible later work and never appear in the current-release Badge editor or rendered side badges.

The fixed Bug Fix button shares the topmost floating control layer with Seeking Filters, Visibility Controls, and Spots, above both navigation bars and map content, without changing its far-right position.
The Spots sheet and its controls render above Seeking Filters, Visibility Controls, Bug Fix, and both navigation bars.
Signup and onboarding never request or store location; location permission is requested only after an explicit location-dependent action.
Every person pin targets the selected profile through focusUserId and the viewer-authorized mutual-map token; unresolved targets never fall back to the signed-in member.

A person pin is bright and actionable only for a mutual who allows precise sharing, is not in Dark Room, and has a valid viewer-authorized token; every other state is dark, disabled, and non-navigable.

Cruushes, normal Messages previews, Feed person cards, and every other compact people listing use one shared UserActivityCapsule style. The heart stays on the left; name and pronouns lead the content; activity metadata stacks; both side badges sit side by side directly under the heart; each badge exposes its meaning on hover; surface content follows the identity block; Delete remains optional in the upper-right. Compact listings do not show vibe tags.
Compact people cards omit vibe capsules. Messages render the last-message preview in the same content slot where Feed renders post text.

Full-screen Cruushes, Messages, Profile View, Profile Edit, Seeking Filters, and Visibility Controls center their tab and count bars against the viewport; embedded and popup layouts retain their current placement.

In desktop Pop-ups mode, opening a normal message thread replaces the Messages list inside the same popup; Back returns to the list, Close dismisses the popup, and Settings plus Close remain at the popup's far-right edge.
Opening Settings from any desktop popup replaces that popup's content inside the same popup. It never opens a second popup. Back returns to the prior popup content.
Desktop popups keep a visible draggable move handle above sticky page headers; Settings and Close sit together at the popup's far-right edge without reserving an empty Bug Fix slot.
Popup headers never reserve or render an internal Bug Fix slot; their normal far-right page action occupies that space while the global Bug Fix control remains outside the popup.
Right-slot desktop popups default flush to the right screen margin and remain constrained to the right half while being dragged.
Notifications supports authenticated owner-only individual deletion and confirmed bulk deletion, updating the visible list and global unread count immediately.
Pulse EKG geometry is vertically centered, reaches both inner heart edges, and is entirely clipped to HEART_PIN_PATH in current-user, seeded Pulse, clustered, and preview states.
Active Ghost Mode and the rotating fly-out use the exact supplied /Volumes/good/ghost-mode-icon-final.svg asset through the shared GhostColoredIcon implementation.
Only missing Badge, Kink, and Vibe menu behavior and required schema support transfer from Cruushv2-visual; source map, Mile High Club location, and general location logic does not transfer.
All user-facing place labels read Spots or spot while internal places tables, APIs, identifiers, component names, and the /places/:placeId route remain compatible.

Seeking, Visibility, and Spots each show no more than one descriptive tagline directly below the header. Visibility says Pick who should not see you. Spots says Public cruising spaces, healthcare clinics, and community spots.
Field labels and placeholders carry their own guidance. No field, control, section, card, or empty state gains helper copy unless Julien explicitly supplies that exact copy.
Spot summaries and details use the current facility categories; Ginger's Bar is shown as Bars, and the legacy Dyke spot tag is never user-visible.
Add spot is one flow. It includes an explicit option to use the current map pin as the suggested Spot's public coordinates instead of a second Pin my map action.

The map loads every published Spot inside the settled map viewport through valid API page sizes; active Spot filters may narrow that viewport dataset, while the first 50-item drawer page never truncates map results.

Spots supports the reviewed 100-mile service area, search, five sorts, staged facility filters, anonymous encrypted suggestions, moderator review, combined timed board-post check-ins, opt-in Who's Here, six-category ratings, and privacy-thresholded Popular times.

The active cruush service area is one shared 100-mile radius centered on New York City. Members may zoom out until the complete service-area edge is visible, while dark blue fog of war obscures everything outside it. Discovery is limited to 50 miles from the member's current location, with Mile High Club fog obscuring the map beyond that browse radius. Trying to browse beyond the radius without Mile High Club offers a direct way to turn on Mile High Club there. While Mile High Club is active, its dropped pin replaces the member's current location for the same 50-mile browse radius and for the Center your location control.
Desktop Spot selection opens the full Spot board popup and mobile selection opens /places/:placeId; hover, click, short-tap, and long-press behavior match the Spots handoff.

One Map Controls dropdown contains Seeking or Mutuals, Visibility, Spots, Pulse, seven-day activity heatmap, location centering, and zoom controls in the approved order without allowing pointer events through to covered markers.
Map Controls triggers and icons increase border, background, icon, and text contrast on hover; hover never makes a control less apparent.
The heatmap is off by default and renders privacy-safe seven-day activity totals as broad area trends; it never mirrors one heat point beneath each current heart pin.
The map loads and mounts only viewer-authorized people and published Spots inside the settled viewport. Pan and zoom refresh both viewport datasets, while applied Spot filters narrow only Spots.
People and Spot clustering remain independent, exact-coordinate people retain spiderfy, cluster selection fits member bounds, and zoom never changes an individual member's display coordinates.
Person heart pins do not show a mutual-relationship side badge; the left side defaults to the profile's Role glyph and the right side defaults to the profile's Position glyph.

Feed message content renders directly below the identity and badge area and uses the same font size as the member name. Basic Feed posts remain text-only, while cruush+ Feed posts can upload and publish up to three policy-compliant photos with approved heart-shaped previews and a full rectangular viewer. Feed photos use the same allowed-content rules as message photos, including multiple subjects and allowed non-human imagery.
One Feed photo renders as one heart, two as welded hearts, and three as a heart cluster; opening any preview shows the full rectangular photo with Close and Report in the upper-right.
Feed photo uploads reuse the approved shared cropper with pan, zoom, continuous rotation, live angle readout, and 90-degree quick rotation controls.

Profile photos may show the uploader, any part of the uploader's body without requiring a face, or the uploader's gear. A profile photo may not contain more than one human subject, and every human subject shown across that profile's photos must be the same person. Feed photos use message-photo rules and may contain multiple subjects or allowed non-human imagery.

Profile photo guidance is a compact four-item bullet list using only this copy: Profile photos may be SFW or NSFW. Use a photo of you or your gear. Add at least one SFW photo if you want people browsing in DL Mode to still see you. You don't have to show your face.

Feed photo explicit classification drives the same DL Mode masking behavior as profile photos, while private message photos continue allowing multiple subjects under the existing message-photo policy.
The cruush Hanky code dialog is substantially larger than its prior compact size and lays out its entries in three columns at supported widths.

No frontend or API development server is started, restarted, stopped, killed, or replaced unless Julien explicitly requests that exact process action. Existing servers may only be inspected and reused.
Remaining docs/todo-2026-08-22.md items are reconciled against current 1.6 source. Only items with claim-matched source and verification evidence are marked complete.

Recently Active loads up to ten viewer-authorized profiles, displays no more than five before hidden-scrollbar horizontal scrolling, supports touch, pointer drag, and mouse-wheel scrolling, and restores the prior translucent black-glass container around the complete open Recently Active unit.

The authoritative to-do keeps the Spots requirements from /Volumes/good/custom-crowds-spots-handoff-2026-08-29.md. Custom saved Crowds are deferred from 1.6 and preserved under /Volumes/good/cruushv2/custom-crowds-20260830.

Transfer the complete newest cruush+ work, including the exact scratch-card interaction, current card visuals, canonical supported-benefit copy, rewards behavior, and explicit post-acceptance dismissal. Locate the authoritative source before editing and never approximate the supplied card.

Rewards shows up to four active Side Quests after Invite people you trust. Claiming one moves it under Recent rewards and reveals the next unclaimed quest. Quests cover simple engagement across profiles, photos, cruushes, Pings, messages, Feed posts, Spots, and Visibility sets. Each Side Quest can be claimed once per member and earns either bonus Pings or one day of cruush+. A member can claim no more than one total Side Quest per local calendar day and no more than two free cruush+ days from Side Quests per local calendar week. Claims are idempotent and never replace paid, lifetime, legacy, referral, coupon, or other promotional access.
The cruush+ time capsule appears immediately below the cruush+ benefits accordion on the Rewards page.

A Spot board post is the check-in action. It requires a message, lets the author choose 1h, 3h, 6h, 12h, or 24h, and provides one optional canonical checkmark to show the member in Who's Here for that same duration. There is no separate check-in button or profile-visibility form.

Spot board posts use the shared Feed and Messages person-card structure, including pronouns, cruush badges, side badges under the heart, post content, expiry, and owner Delete or viewer Report in the upper-right. Compact Spot posts do not show vibe tags.
Spot details expose the opt-in Who's Here list as its own tab alongside the board.

Safe and unambiguous remaining to-do items are implemented in small isolated batches. Items requiring a product decision, merge, migration execution, server control, new visual design, or publication remain explicitly blocked or pending.
